item.title: VMware ESXi Syslog Fields and CIM Add-on - v1.0.0 [New App Release]
item.description:
Platform: Splunk


Release Notes:
- First release.


Short Description:
Search-time fields and CIM mappings (Authentication, Change, Alerts, Web) for VMware ESXi syslog sourcetypes vmware:esxlog:<process>: host agent, SSH and DCUI logins, vSphere tasks with the vCenter user, host audit records, problems and lockouts, plus parsing for more than 100 ESXi processes. Independent project, not affiliated with Broadcom or VMware.


Description:
Search-time fields and CIM mappings for VMware ESXi syslog (sourcetypes vmware:esxlog:, as named by the Splunk Add-on for VMware ESXi Logs). - Authentication: host agent password logins (vSphere API and Host Client), SSH logins and failed DCUI logins, accepted or rejected, with user, source address and method. root logins are also tagged privileged. - Change: vSphere tasks that change something (snapshots, power on/off, reconfigure, register, remove, maintenance mode, services, local accounts, permissions), with the vCenter user who started the task, the action, the object and the command. Read-only API calls are left out. Host audit records (esx.audit.*): SSH or shell enabled and disabled, firewall changes, password changes, account lockouts. - Alerts: host problems (esx.problem.*), account lockouts and repeated login failures. - Web: requests to the host's web services from other machines (envoy-access): method, path, status, bytes, duration, client, TLS version, SOAP action. Also parses more than 100 ESXi processes: header (process, pid, log level, message), the [Originator@6876 sub= opID= user=] block, and process-specific fields: vmkernel modules, storage devices and latency, VM names and actions, HA (Fdm) state, VpxLRO operations, cron and SSH commands, VIB checks, Active Directory messages, etcd and cluster agent fields. Search-time only: install on search heads. Works with ESXi 7 and 8 layouts, classic or ISO timestamps, RFC 3164 or RFC 5424, with or without the syslog header. Independent project, not affiliated with or endorsed by Broadcom or VMware. VMware and ESXi are trademarks of Broadcom Inc.

Release Notes:

Short Description:
Detection engineering, threat exposure, covert-channel hunting and attack chain operations for Splunk Enterprise Security in one app.


Description:
DDA Detection and Defence Atlas App is a single app for use with Splunk Enterprise and Splunk Enterprise Security that brings detection engineering and active defence into one workflow. Detection Fidelity inventories every correlation search and scores it with an explicit policy: MITRE ATT&CK and kill chain mapping, security domain, drilldown, SPL cost and run reliability. SPL Advisor reviews each search line by line with a 33-item best-practice pack. Telemetry Readiness shows whether the data each detection needs is arriving, and Operational Health catches failed, skipped, slow or noisy detections. Threat Exposure Intelligence compares the last 24 hours of Network_Traffic relationships with a 30-day baseline and highlights new, unapproved relationships to critical assets. Attack Story & Covert Intelligence runs four network hunts (beacon periodicity, outbound volume against baseline, low-and-slow transfer, new external peer) and links them with ES risk on the same system and time bucket. Advanced Threat Operations ships 17 intermediate findings and 5 ordered chain correlations (disabled by default) with a 35-day baseline memory, segmentation policy checks and a live case queue. Entity Atlas puts ES risk, findings and relationship novelty for one host, IP address or account on a single timeline. Every module is evidence first and read only: the app never blocks traffic and never changes firewall or ES settings. IMPORTANT - first-time setup is required. Detection Fidelity works right after install. Threat Exposure and Advanced Threat Operations need your own environment data in the operator lookups (domain controllers, privileged accounts, network zones, segment policy, critical assets) and a baseline run; until then their rules and panels return nothing. This is expected, not a fault. The Installation tab and the README list every lookup, an example row and what stays empty without it.

Description:
The Data Source Validator app validates that user-defined data sources are currently returning at least one event in Splunk. Administrators define platforms such as Firewall or EDR, and under each platform create one or more data sources with an SPL search that should return events. A single sequential validation worker executes each data source's search on a schedule or on demand using a dedicated service account with minimal privileges. The app records PASS, FAIL, ERROR, or STALE status for each data source, and platform status rolls up from the status of its enabled child data sources. This provides visibility into which integrations have stopped receiving data. The app targets Splunk Cloud Platform and Splunk Enterprise 9.3 and later.

item.title: SPL Library - v3.8.0 [Version Update]
item.description:
Platform: Splunk


Short Description:
Provides a searchable library interface for storing and managing Splunk queries with category filtering, one-click execution, and KV Store persistence.


Description:
The SPL Library provides a modern interface for storing, searching, and managing Splunk queries within the Splunk environment. The application features a dark card-based user interface that displays saved queries in an organized, searchable format. Users can perform full-text searches across query titles, descriptions, tags, and SPL content, and apply category filters to narrow results by Security, Network, Application, Database, Performance, or Other classifications. Each query card can be expanded to view the complete SPL code, copied to the clipboard with one click, or executed directly in the Splunk Search app. The application stores all queries in the Splunk KV Store, ensuring compatibility with Splunk Cloud deployments. Query management capabilities include adding, editing, and deleting entries through a modal form interface with tag assignment functionality. The application automatically seeds four example queries on initial deployment and records metadata including author information and creation/modification timestamps for each stored query. The architecture avoids custom REST handlers, external dependencies, and inline JavaScript, relying exclusively on Splunk-provided libraries and standard KV Store mechanisms for data persistence.

item.title: DIA Data Integrity App - v2.0.0 [New App Release]
item.description:
Platform: Splunk


Release Notes:
2.0.0 \- First Splunkbase release as "DIA Data Integrity App" (app ID dda_data_integrity). \- New pages: Data Model Fields (CIM field fill rate, empty recommended fields, non-standard and malformed values), Field Anomalies (broken field names, malformed values, timestamp and type problems), Source Detail and Setup & Health. The original dashboard is the Overview. \- New scheduled analysis: CIM field reference read from the installed data models, CIM field profile per data model and source, field anomaly checks per source, time zone offset detection. \- Every setting is a search macro (scope, mapping window default 7 days, summariesonly default true, sample window and sizes, pair limits); the Overview shows p90 job run times with tuning recommendations and lists data models that are not measured. \- Readable only by admin and sc_admin by default, because the lookups contain sample values. \- English user interface and Splunkbase packaging. \- Upgrade from 1.x (app ID DA-DataIntegrity): remove the old app and install this one; the lookups are rebuilt automatically.


Description:
DIA Data Integrity App gives Splunk and data administrators detailed control panels for one question: is the data in every index and sourcetype correct and usable by CIM-based content such as correlation searches, dashboards and Splunk Enterprise Security? Data model mapping, verified: for 28 CIM data models the app runs tstats by index and sourcetype and records which sources really land in each data model. The verdict comes from tstats, not from CIM index macros or tags alone. Acceleration coverage and cim_*_indexes macros are checked too. CIM field profile: for every data model and source the app samples events and measures each CIM field - how often it is filled, how often it only holds placeholders such as unknown or -, and whether its values follow the CIM definition (expected values, number type, port, IP, hash and MAC shapes). Recommended fields that a source never fills are listed per source. Field definitions are read from the data models installed on your search head, so custom models and newer CIM versions are covered automatically. Field anomalies: every extracted field of every source is checked for broken names (generic CEF cs1/cn1 fields with their real name suggested from the label, positional field3 names, values used as field names, case-variant duplicates), malformed values (key=value inside a value, leftover quotes, spaces, unparsed JSON/XML, encoding artefacts), mixed number/text types, mostly empty fields and timestamp fields that cannot be parsed or disagree with _time. Parsing and time: unparsed and partially parsed sources, multi-line and future-dated events, indexing latency and likely time zone offsets. Recommendations for unmapped sources suggest the data model, tags, key CIM fields and the add-on to use. No setup is needed: after install, first-run searches build the analysis automatically within minutes and scheduled searches refresh it every 4 hours. Defaults are light (7 days, acceleration summaries only, 200-300 sampled events per source); every window, sample size and limit is a macro, and the Overview shows the p90 run time of each job with tuning recommendations. The app is read-only for your data and never changes props, transforms, data models or macros.

item.title: DataRunk Alert Enhancer - v1.0.0 [New App Release]
item.description:
Platform: Splunk


Release Notes:
**App version number** 1.0.0 **Release notes** Initial release of the SA-DataRunkAlertEnhancer add-on for Splunk Enterprise Security. This release introduces AI-driven triage automation using Gemini, including the following key features: * **AI-Powered Adaptive Response:** Adds the "Enhance Alert with Gemini AI" alert action to enrich ES findings with automated investigation notes. * **Custom AI Personas:** Role-based analysis with selectable profiles for Blue Team SOC Analysts, Command-Center Analysts, and Anti-Fraud/AML Analysts. * **Knowledge Base Injection (Proto-RAG):** Support for uploading operational playbooks (.txt, .md, .yaml up to 1MB) to strictly guide the LLM's decision-making process. * **Dynamic Context & Value Extraction:** Automatically detects event fields and securely extracts column values to build a highly contextualized analysis payload. * **Autonomous Finding Updates:** Native integration with the ES REST API to autonomously update the incident's Status and Disposition based on the AI's verdict. * **Built-in ROI Dashboard:** Includes the "Gemini Analysis ROI" dashboard to track token consumption, calculate LLM costs, and compare them against estimated human triage savings. * **Security & Guardrails:** Advanced prompt injection protections, ignoring malicious instructions even if present in the uploaded raw data. * **Flexible Configuration:** Supports multi-language output, JSON or Markdown formatting, and custom manual prompts (up to 800 characters) with temperature control.


Short Description:
Enhances Splunk Enterprise Security findings with AI-generated analysis from Google Gemini, automatically generating defensive recommendations and updating incident status and disposition.


Description:
The DataRunk Alert Enhancer integrates Google Gemini AI capabilities with Splunk Enterprise Security to automate incident enrichment and triage. The app enhances ES findings by generating AI-powered defensive recommendations, automatically updating incident status and disposition values, and posting structured LLM responses as investigation notes. It provides an alert action that invokes the Gemini API when detections fire, collecting detection context and producing analysis tailored to the security event. Two custom search commands, postrecord and updatefinding, handle the mechanics of writing notes to ES findings and updating finding metadata through the ES REST API. The app includes a configuration dashboard for managing the Gemini API key and meta-prompt templates, as well as a Gemini Analysis ROI dashboard for tracking usage metrics. Two saved searches orchestrate the posting of LLM responses and finding updates, both disabled by default to allow administrators to validate integration requirements before activation. The app stores LLM responses in the KV Store collections gemini_alert_responses and gemini_meta_prompt, enabling correlation and audit trails. By automating initial incident analysis, the DataRunk Alert Enhancer reduces manual triage workload on security operations teams, particularly for incidents without established playbooks.

Description:
Lookup Workbench is an editor for Splunk lookups that lets you edit CSV lookup files and KV store collections in a spreadsheet-like grid, without hand-editing CSV files or writing outputlookup searches. It is built for teams that maintain lookups together, such as allow-lists and exclusion lists for security detections, asset and identity lists, or mapping tables. Every save of a CSV lookup keeps a backup of the previous version, with who changed it and what changed, so any version can be compared, previewed or restored. If a colleague saved the lookup after you opened it, the app asks what to do instead of silently overwriting their work. The app can run a search, a saved search or import an uploaded CSV export next to the lookup. It shows which results the lookup already matches, using the same matching rules as Splunk's lookup command (WILDCARD, CIDR, case sensitivity). You can add the remaining results as new rows and generalize them with wildcards. Validation warns about entries that Splunk would never match, such as plain IP addresses in CIDR columns. Lookup definitions and permissions are managed in the same place, and all access follows Splunk's own permissions.

The FixTrail DESC AlKashif Add-on for Rapid7 Nexpose collects vulnerability and asset inventory data from Rapid7 Nexpose consoles and writes events structured according to the DESC AlKashif field specification for vulnerability assessment scanners. The add-on imports three primary data types: active vulnerabilities, remediated vulnerabilities, and asset inventory records. Each vulnerability event includes fields such as dest, cve, severity, signature, application, asset_os, vulnerability_status, fixed_time, first_found_time, and cvss_v3. The add-on maps imported data to the CIM Vulnerability and Inventory data models. It extends the import logic of the Rapid7 Nexpose Technology Add-On by adding support for remediated vulnerability tracking and AlKashif field normalization. Administrators configure the add-on by supplying Nexpose console credentials and creating modular input jobs that specify which site IDs to import. Import behavior can be customized to control whether solution data and remediated vulnerabilities are included, and whether imports occur only when new scans complete.

item.title: TA-sensors - v1.0.1 [Version Update]
item.description:
Platform: Splunk


Short Description:
Collects Linux hwmon (lm-sensors class) board health - CPU/core temperatures, fans, voltages, NVMe temps, power - from BMC-less hosts with zero dependencies. Stdlib python3 reads /sys/class/hwmon and emits JSON events, mstats-ready sensors.* metrics, and dashboards.


Description:
TA-sensors brings hardware health monitoring to the machines IPMI can't reach. Consumer desktops, gaming rigs, VMs, SBCs and other BMC-less hosts have no out-of-band management controller, so server-grade hardware telemetry (temperatures, fans, voltages, power) is invisible to Splunk. The Linux kernel already exposes all of it through the hwmon subsystem under /sys/class/hwmon - TA-sensors collects it natively, without a BMC, without ipmitool, and without even the lm-sensors package. Two stdlib-only python3 scripted inputs collect every registered hwmon chip (coretemp/k10temp, acpitz, nvme, r8169, mt7921, amdgpu, vendor drivers, and more): - sensors:status (index=main): one nested-JSON event per cycle with sensor_name, reading, reading_value, units and status for every sensor, including latched _alarm flags. - sensors:metrics (index=metrics): true metric events via METRIC-SCHEMA, named sensors._, ideal for mstats time-series, anomaly alerts and trend dashboards. Milli-scaled sysfs inputs are normalized (temp/in/power/current/humidity /1000, fan raw rpm), duplicate chip names are disambiguated with their hwmon number, and all names are sanitized so metric names stay clean and dashboard-safe. Included dashboards: Sensors Overview (per-host reporting, current readings, alarm table) and Sensors Metrics (CPU cores, temperatures, fans, voltages, power draw, live metric volume). TA-sensors is fully standalone, but pairs with TA-IPMI, which covers BMC-equipped servers - together they give complete hardware observability across a mixed fleet. Free and source-available for personal, educational and evaluation use; commercial use requires a paid license from BentleyPC LLC (see LICENSE).

Description:
The Secutec SecureSight Add-on for Splunk collects your organization's assets and threats through the SecureSight Customer API. The Assets input indexes the asset inventory, including assets that were removed. The Threats input indexes every threat with its status, severity, CVSS score and the affected asset. Both inputs read the API's delta streams on a schedule you choose (every 15 minutes by default). The first run indexes the current state of every asset and threat; after that, a checkpoint makes sure each run only indexes what changed, such as a new threat or a status change, and that nothing is indexed twice or lost after an outage. Threats are mapped to the Vulnerabilities data model of the Common Information Model (CIM), so they work with Splunk Enterprise Security and other CIM-based content right away.

The IP Address Ranges input collects every IP address range from Micetro: containers, subnets and from-to ranges, with utilization, custom properties, DHCP scopes and discovery information. The IP Addresses input collects the IPAM records of every range: state, DNS hosts, DHCP reservations and leases, MAC address, last seen time and custom properties, each tagged with the range it belongs to. The add-on reads the data through the Micetro REST API with a read-only Micetro user and indexes a complete snapshot on every run (daily by default). Free addresses are skipped unless you ask for them, and optional Micetro filter expressions limit what is collected to the ranges, folders and addresses you need. Use the data to enrich security and network events with subnet, location and owner information, find stale or unknown addresses, track subnet utilization and compare DNS and DHCP data with what is seen on the network.

A2Z AI Builder turns a request written in plain language into a working Splunk dashboard, cockpit or alert, for use with Splunk® Enterprise and Splunk Cloud Platform. Building good dashboards and alerts takes time and SPL expertise; this app lets any analyst describe what they need, see the result running live on their own data with their own permissions, refine it by chatting, and deploy it in one click. Short Description:
Consume Apache Kafka, Amazon MSK and Confluent Cloud topics directly into Splunk Cloud Platform or Splunk Enterprise. No Kafka Connect, nothing installed on the Kafka side. SASL/SCRAM, TLS/mTLS, SOCKS5 proxy, consumer group offsets.


Description:
Collecting Kafka topics into Splunk usually requires running and maintaining a separate Kafka Connect cluster, which is not always possible. This add-on removes that intermediary: Splunk itself consumes the topics directly from Apache Kafka, Amazon MSK or Confluent Cloud, with nothing to install on the Kafka side. The add-on connects with SASL_SSL (SCRAM-SHA-512 for Amazon MSK, SCRAM-SHA-256, PLAIN for Confluent Cloud) or TLS/mTLS, supports private certificate authorities and an optional SOCKS5 proxy. Offsets are committed to a standard Kafka consumer group only after events are written to Splunk, giving at-least-once delivery and a consumer lag visible with the usual Kafka tools. It works on Splunk Cloud Platform and Splunk Enterprise.

Short Description:
Scan every installed Splunk app for Python 3.13, jQuery 3.5 and Splunk Cloud vetting blockers, get plain-English explanations, and generate patched packages you can download or deploy to Splunk Cloud (ACS), Splunk Enterprise or Git.


Description:
A2Z Python Upgrade finds and fixes the Python 3.13, jQuery 3.5 and Splunk Cloud (AppInspect) blockers in every app installed on your Splunk platform. Splunk 10.2 introduced the Python 3.13 runtime and removed Node.js, and AppInspect now fails any Python extension point (inputs, search commands, REST handlers, alert actions, lookups) that does not declare python.required with 3.13. Many installed apps, especially unmaintained ones, are no longer compatible. The app scans all installed apps (and, on Splunk Enterprise, deployment server, cluster manager and SHC deployer apps) against 34 rules, explains every finding in plain English with the related AppInspect check, and generates a patched package with all safe fixes applied: python.required, splunklib upgrade, removed Python APIs, Simple XML version 1.1, bundled jQuery, packaging issues. item.title: OTel Fleet Monitor for AWS - v1.2.0 [New App Release]
item.description:
Platform: Splunk


Release Notes:
**1.2.0 — First public release on Splunkbase.** Features \- Inventory of OpenTelemetry Collectors on Amazon EKS and ECS through read-only AWS APIs (ECS, EKS, SSM, STS) and the read-only Kubernetes API of each EKS cluster: DaemonSets, Deployments, StatefulSets, pods, ConfigMaps, OpenTelemetryCollector custom resources and EKS add-ons (ADOT). Clusters without any collector are reported. \- Health: silent collectors (running on AWS but not reporting), dropped data by stage, signal and component, exporter sending-queue saturation. \- Versions: CURRENT / OUTDATED / OBSOLETE / UNSUPPORTED / UNPINNED status per workload, based on a version policy fed by GitHub releases and AWS DescribeAddonVersions. \- Expected vs applied configuration: rules per account, cluster, namespace or workload (version, config hash, required or forbidden components), detection of instances still running an older configuration, best-practice findings including plaintext secrets. \- 9 dashboards (including a Home page with a quick-start guide), 9 alerts shipped disabled, KV store reference data. \- Outbound proxy support: per input, app-wide (Administration > Proxy page, Splunk Cloud friendly), Splunk system proxy or environment variables. Proxy password and AWS secret key are stored encrypted in storage/passwords and masked. **Notes** \- Internal versions 1.0.0 and 1.1.0 were never published on Splunkbase. \- All AWS and Kubernetes calls are read-only. Python 3.7 to 3.14 compatible (Splunk Enterprise 9.x and 10.x, Splunk Cloud Platform).


Short Description:
Inventory, health and configuration drift for OpenTelemetry Collectors on Amazon EKS and ECS, directly in Splunk Platform. Finds silent collectors, dropped telemetry, outdated versions, plaintext secrets and differences between expected and applied collector configuration.


Description:
OpenTelemetry Collectors are now the backbone of telemetry pipelines on AWS, but most teams cannot answer basic questions about their own fleet: How many collectors run on EKS and ECS? Which ones stopped sending data? Which ones drop spans, metrics or logs? Which versions are outdated? Is the configuration that actually runs the one we expect? OTel Fleet Monitor for AWS answers these questions in Splunk Platform (Splunk Enterprise and Splunk Cloud Platform), without requiring Splunk Observability Cloud. 1. Inventory A modular input calls read-only AWS APIs (ECS, EKS, SSM, STS) and the read-only Kubernetes API of each EKS cluster to discover every collector: ECS services and tasks, DaemonSets, Deployments, StatefulSets, pods, ConfigMaps, OpenTelemetryCollector custom resources and EKS add-ons such as ADOT. Clusters without any collector are reported. 2. Health The inventory is cross-checked with the collector internal telemetry (otelcol_* metrics): - Silent collectors: running on AWS but no longer reporting (SILENT, NEVER_REPORTED, NOT_INVENTORIED). - Dropped data: refused, dropped and failed-to-export items by stage, signal and component, plus exporter sending-queue saturation. - Versions: CURRENT, OUTDATED, OBSOLETE, UNSUPPORTED or UNPINNED (latest tag), based on a version policy fed by GitHub releases and on AWS add-on versions. 3. Expected vs applied configuration Define expected rules (version, config hash, required or forbidden components) per account, cluster, namespace or workload. The app compares them with the configuration really applied, detects instances still running an older configuration (previous task definition revision, pods started before the last ConfigMap change) and flags bad practices such as a missing memory_limiter, disabled retry or sending queue, disabled TLS verification and plaintext secrets. Included: 8 dashboards, 9 alerts (shipped disabled), KV store reference data, outbound proxy support. All AWS and Kubernetes calls are read-only; secrets are stored encrypted in Splunk and never indexed.

WeAre Website Monitoring Light shows the availability of the HTTP and HTTPS endpoints checked by the TA-weare-website-monitoring-light add-on. The WeAre Website Monitoring Light add-on collects HTTP and HTTPS endpoint availability metrics from a Splunk heavy forwarder. The add-on probes configured web endpoints and generates structured JSON events containing response times, HTTP status codes, content assertion results, TLS certificate expiration data, and outage or recovery state transitions. Each check produces a weare_website_monitoring_light:check event. When an endpoint changes state between available and unavailable, the add-on emits a weare_website_monitoring_light:transition event. The add-on runs as a modular input on Linux heavy forwarders and supports distributed collection by deploying multiple collector instances in different network locations. It enforces a destination policy that controls which hosts, networks, and ports the forwarder may contact, and supports Basic, Bearer, and custom secret-header authentication schemes. The add-on writes to a custom index and pairs with the companion weare-website-monitoring-light search head app to provide dashboards and search-time field extractions.

item.title: Log10x App - v1.2.5 [New App Release]
item.description:
Platform: Splunk


Release Notes:
\- The field map tool generates maps for Windows Security as classic text (\`WinEventLog:Security\`), FortiGate and Palo Alto Networks, beside Windows Security as rendered XML and CloudTrail. With a FortiGate map, the Network_Traffic data model, \`tstats\` and the Splunk Security Content (ESCU) detections give the same results as on raw events. With a Palo Alto map, the Network_Traffic and Change data models, \`tstats\` and ESCU detections give the same results on compact PAN-OS traffic and system events as on raw ones; threat events are passed whole. \- The field map's \`check\` also counts the compact events indexed without their fields and those Splunk dropped because it could not load the map's lookup file, and fails with the count. When its probe arrives late, \`check\` keeps the template list unless Splunk's log shows events of the map dropped. The new Field Map Dropped Events alert reports dropped events by node every five minutes. \- The new search report, \`bin/tenx_search_report.py\`, reads a search head's saved searches, alerts and dashboards and says which run unchanged when a source moves to compact events, which need \`tx\`, \`txf\` or a field map, and which meet a limit the README states. The report changes nothing and starts no search. \- Word searches through \`tx\`, dashboards and compiled alerts find the events of every stored template, including templates stored in the last few minutes. Outside \`NOT\`, a wildcard inside a word (\`Se\*Privilege\`), \`TERM()\` of part of a longer term and \`CASE()\` of a word with a wildcard inside it match as on the original lines. \- \`tx\` and \`txf\` expand an event whose values begin or end with white space or a carriage return, such as a Windows event with CR LF line ends, to its full text, and a carriage return inside an event comes back in place. \- \`tx\` expands events whose template appears twice in the indexers' copy of the template collection. An event \`tx\` cannot expand keeps its compact text and says why in \`tenx_expand_refused\`. \- The Consume KV search stores every template record indexed since the last one it stored, a burst of new templates included, and its first run after an install or an upgrade reads every template record in the index. \`tx\` and \`txf\` warn when Consume KV failed, is still loading, or has not run for fifteen minutes. \- Alerts compiled in the Compile Alert view find their events when the scheduler runs them, including events of templates whose hash contains \`$\`. The recompile pass rewrites alerts compiled with an earlier version within 15 minutes of the upgrade, unless someone has edited them since. \- An epoch-seconds timestamp with a fraction, such as \`msg\=audit(1723042099.699:13369)\`, expands as written and sets the event's time. \- Beside a heavy forwarder, the Receiver can write compact events to files that the heavy forwarder reads and sends to the indexers with its own outputs, with no HTTP Event Collector or token. The \`\_indexers\` package gives each event back its host, source, index and time, and field maps run on the heavy forwarder. \- \`tx\` expands the events a FortiGate field map leaves under the compact sourcetype, such as FortiGate lines the add-on does not type, and a field map keeps the time of an event marked \`tenx_time\=sender\`. \- \`tx\` and \`txf\` run inside \`| union \[...]\`, in a search, a dashboard panel and a saved search, as they do inside \`multisearch\`, \`append\` and \`join\`. \- A search that holds more than one \`tx\` or \`txf\`, such as two arms of a \`multisearch\` or \`union\`, finds every event of each arm. \- \`| tx\` and \`| tenxsearch\` return their events inside \`append\`, \`join\` and \`union\`, and an unexpected error shows on the search instead of an empty result. \- Requires the Log10x Receiver at release 1.1.181 or later and Splunk Enterprise 9.4 through 10.6. After upgrading where a field map is installed, give the role of the token \`activate\` and \`check\` use search access to \`\_internal\`, and schedule \`check\` every minute. A map that \`gen\` generates again after the upgrade can carry a new index-time rule; install both of its apps again whole before running \`activate\`.


Short Description:
Send Splunk the logs that sampling and filters keep out to fit the license, on that same license. Compact events take a fraction of the volume and expand back byte-identical at search time; classic dashboards keep their SPL, and one command covers the search bar, saved searches, alerts and the REST API.


Description:
With the Log10x App, Splunk can index compact log events and still search, chart and alert on the original lines. The 10x Receiver stores each event as a template hash plus the values that change, so a stream of repeated patterns takes less of the license. On the OpenTelemetry demo, Splunk's license meter counted 63.91% fewer bytes, encoded events and templates included, and every line expanded back byte-identical with the Receiver settings in the installation steps (measurement: https://github.com/log-10x/benchmarks/tree/main/splunk-license). The same license then holds more: sources that were sampled, filtered or kept out of Splunk to stay under the limit can come back, or the license can be smaller. To search by what the lines say, write the tx macro in front of an ordinary search: index=my_index `tx` "payment failed" NOT retry. It runs as native SPL in the search bar, Dashboard Studio, saved searches and alerts, and NOT, OR, groups, phrases, field conditions, and values such as IP addresses and hostnames behave as they do on the original data. Classic dashboards keep their SPL: the browser sends each panel's search to the app, which rewrites it on the server. An alert created in the app's Compile Alert view is compiled once into a native saved search. The 10x Receiver produces compact events, and it is free on up to 10 nodes (https://www.log10x.com/pricing). No sign-up is required: with no license token it runs the full product on up to 10 nodes, air-gapped, with no expiry (https://doc.log10x.com/manage/license/). The app itself is open source under the MIT license.

item.title: Riskability - v1.5.1 [Version Update]
item.description:
Platform: Splunk


Release Notes:
# Riskability 1.5.1 What changed since 1.4.1, the version on Splunkbase today. Grouped by what you will notice, not by commit. Nothing has been removed that you were using. ## In one paragraph 1.5.1 adds an Executive summary page that prints as three A4 landscape sheets, a count of new findings that opens the list behind it, and rebuilds the Routes page around the question it was always meant to answer: of the jumps the firewall has seen, which could an attacker actually take, and how far. Every jump is now graded by what taking it would need, a crash-only flaw no longer counts as a way in, and the graph is walked once an hour so it draws an estate of thousands. It also fixes a Routes page where every click said "No results found", and a Feed administration page that looked idle while an import was most of the way through. ## New: Executive summary A page for the people who ask how exposed the organisation is, in the order they ask it: known exploited vulnerabilities open, of those how many answer the network, systems with an open vulnerability, risks consciously accepted, how long serious findings stay open, and how far to trust the figures. Then the reachability matrix, the severity ring, thirty days of movement and the five things to fix first. Every figure is the linked page's own query against the same hourly roll-ups, so a number here always matches the page it links to. There is no composite score, because the app cannot defend one. Print or save as PDF. Splunk's Export to PDF leaves out every custom chart, and an air-gapped search head has no server-side renderer, so the page prints in the reader's own browser: three landscape sheets, always the same shape, with the charts redrawn as vector graphics in a light palette so they stay sharp at any size. Checked in Chromium-based browsers and in Safari; in Safari, pick landscape in the print dialog. ## New: a count of new findings, and the list behind it Start here has a New findings tile: open findings first reported in the last seven days, accepted risks left out, at every confidence. Click the number and Findings opens on those findings, through two new filters, First reported (24 hours, 7 days, 30 days or any time) and Accepted risks (shown or hidden), and a First reported column. New means the first time the app reported the finding, not when the host's inventory was collected. A feed update that flags software nobody has touched in months produces findings that are new today, and those are the ones this tile exists for. Findings recorded before this release have no such date and count by their inventory date instead, which is never later than the truth, so nothing old is passed off as new. ## Routes: graded by what an attacker would need A permitted flow is a path, not an exploit, and the page used to draw every jump the same way, coloured by known-exploited and EPSS, which say nothing about whether a flaw can be reached over this wire. Every jump is now graded from the CVSS vectors of the findings open on the listener it lands on: * CVE-enabled, solid red: reachable over the network, with no account and no user action, and a high impact on confidentiality or integrity. That is the shape of code execution, an authentication bypass or stolen secrets. * Needs a foothold, solid amber: reachable, but it wants credentials or a click. * Unrated, dashed amber: an open finding has no CVSS vector, so the app cannot say. * Permitted only, dashed grey: nothing usable over the network is open there, so the jump needs a zero-day or permissions. A flaw whose only impact is availability opens no jump. CVE-2024-0760 in BIND, a TCP flood that makes the server unstable while it lasts, can crash the listener but cannot put anyone on the host, and neither can HTTP/2 Rapid Reset, so a DNS or web server carrying only those is not drawn as a way in. A low impact alone, a minor leak or change, does not open one either. The findings panel says which of these each CVE is, in an "Over the wire" column: no foothold needed, needs credentials or a click, only to take it down, only a minor leak or change. Every host an attacker can reach from an entry point on CVE-enabled jumps alone is ringed red. A new table lists every path from an entry point, worst first: how many jumps, how far the CVE-only stretch goes, the jump where it stops, and the CVEs behind each jump. The software is on the jump. Each jump is labelled with its protocol, the port it landed on and the software listening there, the first jump from an entry point included. Hovering a jump lists every port it was seen on and what is open behind each, and clicking it opens the findings on those ports rather than the whole host's. ## Routes: drawn at estate size The page used to walk the graph inside its own search on every load, which worked on fifteen hosts and would have taken minutes on five thousand, and hit a limits.conf ceiling before that without saying so. An hourly job now walks it once, with a breadth-first search in a dedicated search command, and the page reads the result. It opens on CVE-enabled jumps and twenty-five hosts per hop, keeps the worst, and says how many it left out. Paths are capped by the job, two thousand at most, and every row says when a cap cut the list. The panel grows with the densest hop instead of packing a large graph into 640 pixels, and a panel resized in the dashboard editor redraws at its new height without a reload. ## Fixed Every click on the Routes graph said "No results found". The click reported its kind with the column prefix still on it, and the findings search compared that against the bare kind. Every edge tooltip on Routes read "N CVEs through this hop" with N being the session count. The label and class were built and then dropped before the chart drew them. Feed administration looked idle during an import. The staged-bundles list redraws every few seconds, and the bundle being imported came back each time with a fresh Import button, so it read as "nothing started" while the import was most of the way through. That bundle now says it is importing and cannot be deleted mid-import, no other bundle can start an import until it finishes, and the percentage counts advisories as well as ranges, so it no longer sits at 99 percent for the whole advisory phase. Explain in depth was refused on Splunk Free. Free has no access control and reports no capabilities for anyone, which the AI page read as "not allowed". On a licensed Splunk the riskability_ai_explain capability decides, exactly as before. On a CVE's page, "Matching hosts in this fleet" came seventh, after five panels of feed text. It now follows the headline figures directly.


Short Description:
Correlate the software your fleet already reports against offline CVE databases on a search head with no internet access. Ranks findings by exploitation likelihood and by whether the network can actually reach them. Track software that is already or soon becoming End Of Life!


Description:
Most vulnerability tooling cannot run where it is needed most. A search head with no route to the internet cannot call an API, pull a feed on a schedule or fetch a score on demand. Riskability is built for that machine. It takes the software inventory your hosts already report, correlates it against databases you carry across the air gap yourself, and answers what a CVE count never does: of everything found, what should somebody do tonight? CVSS says how bad a flaw would be if exploited, not how likely that is, and never whether your copy is reachable. WHAT THIS APP ADDS Exploitation likelihood. Findings are ranked by EPSS, the published probability of exploitation in the wild, and by the CISA KEV catalogue of vulnerabilities already exploited. Both arrive in the feed you import, never fetched live. Reachability, measured on the host. The collector reports listening ports and the process behind each, so findings answering a network address are separated from those answering only loopback or nothing. On a test fleet that turned 10,206 open findings into 11 that answer the network. It reorders the work. It never shortens it. Reachability, observed at the boundary. With your firewall logs in Splunk, the app can also say whether a permitted flow from the internet or an admin network has actually reached a port, and draw the jumps from entry point to the findings at the end. A site without firewall logs loses nothing. End of support. A CVE says a thing is broken; end of support says nobody will fix it again, which no advisory states. The app names software with no supported release. Rules your fleet needs. A risk the scoring signals cannot see can be written as a rule raising a finding one tier. Rules ship off, and a replay shows what each would move first. Optional AI explanation. A model on your own hardware writes the reasoning beside each finding: why it ranks where it does, what to do, which ATT&CK techniques apply. The score is arithmetic from measured facts and the model cannot change it. Where an answer contradicts the evidence, the row says so. WHAT IT REFUSES TO GUESS Every finding carries a confidence level describing the evidence, not the severity. A distribution that backports fixes without changing the version is reported as informational rather than asserted. A Coverage dashboard lists what the data cannot speak to, because a gap in visibility is not an absence of risk. Accepted risks go to an audit index written once, never rewritten. NO UNINTENTIONAL DATA OUT Nothing goes out unless you set up AI, and the recommended shape is a model in the same location as this Splunk instance, so nothing leaves the organisation. You build a feed bundle on a connected machine, carry it across and import it.

Release Notes:
Vyrux 1.1.0 is the largest release yet: a new way to collect logs, scans that hold up on the biggest estates, and a console that reads as one product. **New: API Studio** - Collect from any REST API that has no Splunk add-on. Paste the vendor's documentation and Chuka writes the collector, then lists anything the documentation does not say. - One tested collector engine: API keys, basic, bearer, OAuth client credentials, OAuth with a one-time sign-in and client certificates, with every common paging style, new events only, duplicates removed and rate limits honoured. - A collector turns on only after it passes a test on the real API, including a restart that must lose and repeat nothing. Credentials go only to the host they were entered for. - Runs on the search head, one cluster member at a time, or on a heavy forwarder. Health, field changes and failures are shown and alerted, and a collector running in two places is caught. - One add-on gives the ad hoc search head the same fields, CIM mapping and tags as the Enterprise Security search head. **Parsing Studio** - CSV logs with no header line: every column in its place, named in place or from the vendor's documented layout, and deployed so a quoted comma stays in one field. - A deployment that fails part way is undone, and a rollback restores what was there before. **Scale and reliability** - Scans grow with the size of the estate, not its square. Tested on a model estate of 10,000 sourcetypes and 5,000 saved searches. - Background reads return every row, and large scans are kept compressed, so later visits open at once. - An alert fires again when a fault comes back, and a mass failure arrives as one message. - Two people working on one issue no longer overwrite each other. **Trust** - A Vyrux admin manages the licence, connectors and proxy without a Splunk admin role. - Field settings Chuka writes are never run as searches. Evidence and the Vyrux log are protected from change by members. **A calmer, consistent console** - One main button style, one date format, one colour scale for scores, readable banners, text on one type scale, and help on every figure. - Every word reviewed: true statements only, empty states and errors that say what to do next, and one term for one thing. The full guide, with every change in this release: https://vyrux-docs.pages.dev


Short Description:
Know that your Splunk works. Prove your logs arrive, your rules can fire and your ATT&CK coverage is real, then fix every gap.


Description:
Every SOC pays for its logs and writes its detections. Few can show, on any given morning, that the logs arrived, that the parsing still holds and that the correlation searches they rely on can still fire. That gap stays hidden until an incident review finds it. Vyrux closes it inside your own Splunk. Every 15 minutes it checks each log, each rule and each ATT&CK technique you count as covered. It explains what broke, traces it to its root cause and turns it into owned work, with a fix your engineers test before anything changes in Splunk. Chuka, the built-in AI detection engineer, explains, fixes and drafts rules from your real fields, and Splunk checks everything Chuka writes before anyone can use it. Vyrux is one app on the search head, including the Enterprise Security search head. It is not SaaS. It reads Splunk with each person's own permissions, keeps its records in your KV store, and your log data stays with you.

Release Notes:

A saved search or dashboard that calls one needs \`| chironunpack raw\` instead, or the macros installed by hand. \- A field joined into a value with eval's \`.\` operator (\`eval key\=host."|".level\`) is now extracted correctly on consolidated data. Requires data written by the Chiron platform and Splunk Enterprise 10.0 on Linux (x86-64 or aarch64).


Short Description:

typed URL passwords are refused. - Editing a dashboard the agent built changes that dashboard; a dashboard can show two time windows. - Users with only the user role, matched by an Organisation, are no longer shown as unassigned. - Tools disabled for an Organisation stay disabled for every role; unreadable settings offer no tools. - Time words such as "today" or "last week" set a dashboard's time range. **Upgrade notes** - Re-sign your scheduled jobs once on the Unattended tab; until then they do not run. - A job set up outside the Unattended tab must be recreated there. **Known issues** - On Splunk 10.6, limit `_internal` to administrators: KV Store records can land there. - A Gemini connection cannot run unattended agents in this version. --- ## 2.7.6 A maintenance release: dashboards built in one compile call, a clearer Audit tab, safe behaviour when the KV Store does not answer, and fixes to knowledge, agents and dashboards. **New** - Build a Simple XML dashboard compiles in one call; empty panels are reported, not blocked. - Build a Dashboard Studio dashboard (admin preview): brand canvas, 1920 wallboard, verification strip; Splunk 10.2, 10.4. - Charts over time zoom the time range: drag in Dashboard Studio, click in Simple XML. - The Data quality header on compiled dashboards includes Splunk's ingestion check. - A banner says when Org DFLT has no audit index. - Dashboard Studio dashboards can have tabs; a panel can open another tab (Splunk 10.2, 10.4). - The Dashboard Studio JSON builder is retired; use the Build a Dashboard Studio dashboard agent. - The Audit tab shows one row per request, with a Model calls column. - An unattended agent run is one Audit row, labelled Agent run. - The Audit tab shows up to 200 rows and says when there are more. - Scheduled and triggered agent runs use their agent's skills. **Fixed** - Stop ends a dashboard build; nothing more is written after it. - A drilldown token without a default is refused at publish. - The audit check confirms written entries reliably, also right after a restart. - When the KV Store does not answer, background jobs say so and overwrite nothing. - A deleted default Organisation or Business Unit is restored at startup. - An agent job with an unusable tool list is refused when you save it. - An alert that fires again after a failed agent run starts a new run. - Only Operational knowledge is used; a deleted shipped rule or entry stays deleted. - A knowledge weight, priority or threshold of 0 is used as 0. - A knowledge search answers at its deadline, even when a source is slow. - A dashboard with a base search handles a refused change without looping. - A saved search that claims to count errors or warnings must select them. - Your request never blocks a save; the answer says what the search does not filter on. - Overwrite set to "true" asks you to confirm, then replaces the dashboard. - The Tool calls panel shows when it waits for your approval. - Outcomes, Resource Consumption, Knowledge Layer Health and RCA Investigation show correct figures. - Observability pack tools are installed once per change, never twice. **Known issue** - Splunk 10.6 is not yet supported: `_internal` can hold conversations and the licence key. Use 10.4.x. --- ## 2.7.5 A maintenance release: connections keep who may use them, searches are checked faster, and costs are shown honestly. **New** - AI Activity: a dashboard of agent runs, their tool calls and costs. - Administrators choose which models the Console offers. - "Refresh prices" updates model prices from a community price list. - A cleaner model picker: one label per model, chat models only. - A dashboard made with the dashboard builder carries a Data quality row. - All the app's dashboards share one style. - Adjutant AI chooses how to run a search-time filter, and says which it used. **Fixed** - The connection list offers exactly the connections you may use. - Settings and the setup wizard show who may use a connection as stored. - Editing a connection in Settings keeps who may use it; check connections edited before 2.7.5. - Replacing an existing dashboard always asks you first. - An unknown cost shows as "cost unknown", never $0.0000. - Prompt-cache writes and dated model names are priced correctly. - Custom tools work when an agent calls them on Splunk 10.x. - A search runs over the time range it names itself. - Checking searches for rare events, and publishing dashboards, are quicker. - Dashboard panel checks look further back for each panel. - The Tool calls panel marks only what needs your attention. - The Outcome Ledger shows median time to verdict, and "No reviews yet" when there are none. **Known issue** - Models you registered by hand before 2.7.5: register them again to price cache writes. --- ## 2.7.0 Governed agents, a panel to watch and stop each request, stricter checks, and multi-source reconciliation as a Preview. **New** - Playbooks are now agents, switched on per mode: triggered, scheduled, integration or MCP. - The Tool calls panel shows each step of a request; you can stop it. - Edit dialogs keep your work and behave the same everywhere. - Connect a self-hosted or in-house model as an OpenAI-compatible endpoint. - Reconcile several sources into one reviewed view (Preview). - Write the reconciled view to ServiceNow, after a preview and approval (Preview). - Records deleted in ServiceNow outside Adjutant AI are reported. - Compare, check and save contract versions on the integration page. - A count over indexed fields runs as tstats, and is much faster. - Large searches answer from a sample when that gives the same answer, and say so. - A proof dashboard is built only when you ask for one. - Unattended runs write a searchable log. - The support bundle shows where a run spent its time. **Changed** - Integrations need an Enterprise or MSP licence; nothing is deleted. - The four MCP tools are renamed; update connected MCP clients. - A user in no Organisation is refused everywhere. - Only the requester or an administrator may approve a blocked integration write. - A run that names no LLM connection stops before any model call. **Fixed** - Editing an agent or skill keeps who can see it. - A custom tool's connection details are shown to administrators only. - Domain Workspace model edits stay within their own Organisation. - Dashboards render for non-admin users on Splunk 10.4. - Searches that cannot work, such as tstats on a search-time field, are refused. - An AI Toolkit model is not saved from too few or unvarying training rows. - Backups of collections over 5,000 rows contain each row exactly once. - Overwriting a shared dashboard, saved search or alert updates it, not a private copy. - The sign-in check passes only when it recognises the provider. - A ServiceNow integration reads only the records its mapping selects. - A run in which ServiceNow refused a record is not reported as verified. --- ## Earlier releases - **2.7.1 – 2.7.3** — Maintenance releases: dashboard publishing on Splunk 10.2, connections behind a corporate proxy, the setup wizard. - **2.5** — Setup wizard, one connection for several tenants, private endpoints, a readable RCA report. - **2.4** — Integrations, connectivity fixes, and a data-correctness fix. - **2.2** — Explain a SPL search. - **2.1** — The Fraud capability. - **2.0** — ITSI Root Cause Analysis, resource-consumption monitoring, memory and governed integrations. - **1.8** — CIM Coverage Audit, Outcome Ledger, OCSF export, content packs, security hardening. - **1.7** — ServiceNow integration. - **1.5** — Data Foundation and MCP OAuth. - **1.0 – 1.4** — Knowledge layer, multi-tenancy, audit logging and edition licensing.

Platform: Splunk


Release Notes:
Akamai MFA is regularly updated to deliver new features and improvements.


Description:
Akamai MFA is a next-generation MFA solution that features a phishing-resistant push authentication factor utilizing FIDO2. Akamai MFA couples the proven security of FIDO2 with the familiar and frictionless user experience of a mobile push — removing the need for costly and cumbersome hardware security keys. Deployed on the Akamai Intelligent Edge Platform, Akamai MFA can be activated and managed centrally via Enterprise Center with global reach and scale for resilience and performance. The Akamai MFA App for Splunk allows customers to ingest authentication events and other data from the Akamai MFA service into Splunk for further analysis and correlation.
